correctness.rationale: The exact lift derivative is \(F'(x)=1+4\pi a b^2\cos(2\pi x)(r-\sin(2\pi x))\), with the sign of \(\Omega\) removed by conjugacy. Its stationary phases reduce to \(2u^2-ru-1=0\); these yield at most two negative wells. Ordering their depths and counting negative-level intersections proves every critical-point regime and the included homeomorphism endpoint, including double tangencies. Taylor expansion proves both the \(3/2\)-power secondary-threshold divergence and square-root separation of the pairs. The packaged program checks 144 finite identities and samples; no infinite conclusion rests on it.

originality.rationale: The source (2022) expressly leaves the global criticality boundary unsolved, while its \(F'=1\) fixed-point bifurcation conditions differ from global \(F'=0\) phase geometry. The present proof determines all critical-zero counts, two exact threshold surfaces, their coalescence and the \(3/2\)-power blow-up. General results on other circle maps do not immediately entail this parameter-specific statement, though unindexed or inaccessible covering work remains possible.
residual_risks: The full 2025 Simile Baroni et al. article could not be examined; an unobserved exact fold calculation there remains possible even though its accessible abstract centers other results.
Unindexed classical two-harmonic circle-map calculations might imply or explicitly reproduce the thresholds; a negative database search is not a novelty certificate.
Some broad secondary sources were compared by abstract/selected sections rather than complete text, and independent priority assessment remains outstanding.

value.rationale: The exact injectivity boundary is motivated by the originating dynamics paper, which specifically calls the criticality curve difficult to locate. The result closes the complete natural parameter classification, including two-stage turning-set transitions, simultaneous births at \(\Omega=0\), and the \(3/2\)-power edge singularity. This is a structural diagnosis beyond known fixed-point saddle-node curves, not merely a selected example. Chaotic-onset claims are excluded.
